objectives.outcome: Use common everyday verb–noun combinations naturally.
Understand and use the descriptive adjectives assessed in the Quiz, including their English meanings and Simplified Chinese equivalents.
Choose a, an and the using identifiability and initial sounds, with the vocabulary used in lesson examples.
Distinguish countable and uncountable nouns and use their quantity expressions, including advice, information, equipment and furniture.
Recognise subject, verb and object roles, basic word order and simple question patterns.
Use the present simple for routines and repeated actions, including third-person singular forms.
Recognise and use common word partnerships such as make a decision and take responsibility.
Use first, second and related conditional clauses, including unless and even if, and understand hypothetical and realistic situations.
Understand and use phrasal verbs including give up, put off, look after and run into.
Use perfect forms to connect earlier actions with a later reference point.
Recognise word families, prefixes, suffixes and commonly confused forms such as affect/effect and convince/convincing.
Qualify claims and understand related academic vocabulary used to describe certainty, evidence, effects and causation.
Recognise and use formal inversion after negative or restrictive expressions.
Interpret and form mixed conditionals connecting unreal past conditions with present results, or present conditions with past results.
Interpret the figurative meanings of idioms used in the lesson and Quiz.
Distinguish near-synonyms and precise vocabulary for tone, evidence, judgement and disclosure.
Choose appropriate greetings, thanks, apologies and polite expressions for common everyday interactions.
Recognise common public places and use basic vocabulary for finding and describing locations.
Form yes/no questions, WH-questions and negative statements using be, do, does and did.
Form present, past and present-perfect passive structures and decide when the agent should be included.
Report statements, questions and requests with appropriate word order, tense and reference changes.
